metadata.hardware_requirements: "computing server with NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores)"

nodes_source.source_quote: The data used to support the results of this study are available from the corresponding author upon request.
nodes_source.description: Empirical traffic video data and traffic volumes collected from 7:50 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. on the freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao in Shandong, China.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Authors explicitly state that the data is available upon request from the corresponding author, but no public link or DOI is provided.

nodes_process.source_quote: Three consecutive frames of the traffic video in the controlled area are needed as the observation input of each decision time step.
nodes_process.description: The real-world traffic network is simulated using SUMO. Three consecutive traffic video frames are extracted, zoomed, and down-sampled to 4x512 pixels, then stacked to form the state observation.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, simulator named but no version, parameter values explicitly defined.

nodes_process.source_quote: consists of three convolutional neural network (CNN) layers and one full connection (FC) layer for each output layer.
nodes_process.description: Construct a multitask deep Q-network to predict Q-values, average speed, and queue length. The architecture uses 3 CNN layers followed by fully connected layers with ReLU activations.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, detailed network architecture shown in Figure 7, no specific deep learning framework named.

nodes_process.source_quote: The gradient-based algorithm Adam [28] is used to update wi to minimize the loss function.
nodes_process.description: Train the DRL agent using Q-learning with experience replay, target network freezing, an epsilon-greedy strategy, and the Adam optimizer over 4200 training steps.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, algorithm strictly defined, optimizer named, comprehensive hyperparameters in Table 1.

nodes_process.source_quote: KR = 90 and KP = 50 are two regulator parameters in PI-ALINEA, which are fine-tuned to minimize mean travel times
nodes_process.description: Configure the PI-ALINEA baseline ramp metering algorithm using proportional and integral parameters to maintain a target mainline occupancy of 16 percent.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, formula and required mathematical constants explicitly stated in text.

nodes_process.source_quote: each scenario is evaluated in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_process.description: Evaluate No-control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL strategies across 20 simulation runs initialized with varied random seeds. Measure quantiles of mainline travel time and map spatial-temporal mean speeds.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, number of repeated runs given, specific random seeds are not provided.

nodes_process.node_name: Queue Length and Traffic Flow Evaluation
nodes_process.source_quote: Figure 11 presents the Q1, Q2, and Q3 of the queue lengths at the on-ramp in three scenarios.
nodes_process.description: Analyze the on-ramp vehicle queue lengths and downstream mainline traffic volumes resulting from the three control strategies over the 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, direct result extraction from the simulated scenarios in meth_05.

nodes_process.source_quote: A perturbation analysis is conducted to evaluate the impact of information contained in video data.
nodes_process.description: Divide the video control area into 8 subareas. Sequentially mask information from each subarea and run 20 simulations per configuration to evaluate impact on vehicle travel times.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, procedure and grid divisions specified, parameter values listed.

nodes_sink.source_quote: The training process, presented in Figure 8, can be finished in less than 24 hours on a computing server
nodes_sink.description: Convergence curves showing episode reward and mean travel time over 1,000,000 training frames.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: RL method and hyperparameters are detailed, but relies on proprietary empirical traffic data fed into SUMO, available only upon request.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 9 presents the Q1 (25%), Q2 (50%), and Q3 (75%) of the travel times in the mainline for three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Quartiles (Q1, median, Q3) of mainline vehicle travel times for no-control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL scenarios over time.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Evaluation setup and baseline parameters are provided. Base traffic data required for simulation is not openly accessible.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Table 2 presents mean vehicle travel times in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_sink.description: Mean vehicle travel times across 20 independent simulation experiments initialized with different random seeds for three control scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Random seed initialization mentioned, scenarios clear. Underlying empirical traffic profiles needed to fully reproduce the simulation outcomes.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 10 presents the temporal-spatial distribution of the mean speeds along the mainline.
nodes_sink.description: Spatiotemporal heatmaps of mean speeds along the mainline for no-control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Direct visualization of SUMO simulation trajectories. Reproducibility capped by closed input traffic dataset.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 11 presents the Q1, Q2, and Q3 of the queue lengths at the on-ramp in three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Quartiles of on-ramp queue lengths over the simulation period for no control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Clearly aggregates simulation queue outputs, but inherits the data availability limitation of the simulation setup.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 12 presents the mean queue lengths at the on-ramp and the red ratios (i.e., the proportion of the red phase in the simulation time) in each simulation
nodes_sink.description: Scatter plot correlating queue length and red ratio for PI-ALINEA and DRL methods.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Well-defined metrics computed from simulation outputs. Base traffic demand profiles are closed.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 13 presents the queue lengths at the on-ramp and the occupancy downstream of the merging area for the two ramp metering methods.
nodes_sink.description: Time series comparing on-ramp queue length against downstream occupancy for PI-ALINEA and DRL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Clear comparison of simulated metrics, subject to identical raw data restrictions.

nodes_sink.source_quote: The better performance of the proposed DRL method is further revealed when considering traffic flows downstream of the merge area, which is demonstrated in Figure 14.
nodes_sink.description: Box plots of downstream traffic volume over time intervals for the three scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Transparent boxplot visualization of SUMO output flows, but base traffic dataset limits independent reproduction.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 16 presents the box plot of travel time when the information of different subareas is removed, and the baseline is the result of experiments that take original data as input.
nodes_sink.description: Perturbation analysis showing mainline travel time distributions when specific subareas' input data are masked.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Ablation process logically described. Relies on the same closed empirical dataset.
